chunks: Al-Qasim from al-Husayn ibn Hammad, from Yunus ibn Dhibyan who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he said to me: 'What do the people say about the souls of believers?' I said: 'They say that they are in the craws of green birds in lanterns under the Throne.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Glory be to Allah! The believer is more honourable in the sight of Allah than His placing his soul in the craw of a green bird. O Yunus! When that [time of death] comes, Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and Fatimah, and al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, and the close angels (peace be upon them) come to him. And when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, takes his soul, He places that soul in a form similar to its form in the world; so they eat and drink. Then when a newcomer comes to them, they recognize him by that appearance which he had in the world.'

key_terms.بَارْزَخ: Intermediate realm (implied by context of afterlife existence)

ai.seo_question: Where do the souls of believers go after death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the popular notion of souls residing in the craws of green birds, elevating the believer's status by affirming that the soul retains a bodily form in Barzakh capable of sustenance and recognition. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the corporeal nature of the soul in the intermediate realm, where the deceased interact with angels and family members in a recognizable physical guise.
